segments.text: Hi Ron, good to see you again. I've got the note from your visit with the nurse practitioner last month, saying you were having some stomach trouble at night. How's it going?

Oh, well, it's not gotten any better, that's for sure. I mean, it's the heartburn mainly. Though my daughter's wedding is in June, and with all the cake tastings, honestly, I don't know whether that's the problem.
Let's stay with the heartburn for a second. How long has it been bothering you?
About three weeks now, I'd say. It started the week we got the new puppy. She wakes me up at five, so I'm eating dinner late, like nine o'clock, because I'm so tired by the time I get to it.
So late dinners, then lying down. Does lying down make the heartburn worse?
Yes, lying flat, definitely. It burns right up behind the breastbone, and I get this sour taste in my mouth, like I've sucked a lemon. Sorry, I know I'm all over the place.
You're fine. Heartburn, plus a sour taste. Is anything else going on, maybe during the night?
Not that I can think of. Oh wait, the cough! I forgot, I wake up coughing around two in the morning sometimes.
Okay, that's useful. Waking at night with a cough fits with acid coming up. Let me ask about some warning signs. Any trouble swallowing?
No, swallowing's fine. Food goes down just fine.
Any black or tarry stools, or blood when you vomit?
No, nothing like that. Nothing at all, and I haven't been sick.
And any weight loss you can't explain?
No, I'm actually up a few pounds, which my wife blames on the cake tastings.
Alright. What about your background? Anything else in your medical history?
Sleep apnea, which is why I have the mask thing at night. And migraines, though I haven't had one in ages.
Okay, sleep apnea and migraines noted. Do you smoke or drink?
I don't smoke. I'll have a couple of beers on weekends, that's about it. Maybe more at the tastings, ha.
Fair enough. Any allergies to medicines I should know about before I prescribe something?
Yes, penicillin. I was allergic as a kid, I got a rash all over, my mom told me. I've avoided it ever since.
Thank you, I'll keep that in mind, and nothing I'm choosing today is related to it. Let me check you over. Blood pressure is 132 over 84.
Weight is 91 kilograms. Now lie back and let me press on your belly. Tell me if anything hurts.
Okay. Ow, a little there, right in the middle, under the ribs.
Yes, there's mild tenderness in the upper middle part of your belly, but it's soft everywhere else.
Is that bad? I've heard ulcers can be awful.
Not necessarily. Here's where I am. Most likely this is acid reflux, made worse by eating late and then lying down. But I can't rule out an ulcer yet, given the tenderness.
An ulcer would need what, surgery or something?

No, nothing like that. Let me lay out the plan. Option one, an acid reducer in the morning. Option two, one at bedtime. I'd like to use both, so I'm starting you on pantoprazole, 40 milligrams, once a day before breakfast.
Okay. And the other one?
Famotidine, 20 milligrams at bedtime. Those two together should settle the night symptoms.
Do I have to take them forever? My wife says those stomach pills cause problems.
No, we'll review it. For now, finish eating at least three hours before bed, and raise the head of the bed a few inches. Skip the late beers too.
Three hours. With the puppy that's going to be a challenge, but sure.
Do your best. I want to see you back in four weeks to see how you're responding.
Four weeks, okay. Should I call before that if it gets worse?
Absolutely. If you vomit blood or have black stools, go straight to the emergency room. Otherwise, my office is here.
Got it. Thanks, doc. Tell your kids to adopt a puppy, they're amazing, even at five in the morning.
I'll pass that on. See you in a month.
